note: The entry follows Holmgren's 1910 original description (queen, soldier and worker). The original is a library OCR text of a BHL scan (Zenodo/Plazi mirror); the German original description was read line by line; figures that the OCR scrambled beyond confirmation are not listed.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: (The original describes only the queen.) Very similar to Eutermes chaquimayensis, of the same colour, the head covered with rather dense white hairs, of the same size; the occiput possibly slightly longer and the pronotum slightly broader.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Body length 3—3.5 mm; head length mode 1.40—1.45 mm (the range printed in the original is damaged by OCR as '1.55—1.55', so only the mode is given); head width 0.75—0.95 mm (51 specimens measured). Head brown, paler around the antennae and at the tip of the nasus; antennae, legs and the rest of the body rusty yellow. Head with a few bristles at the base of the nasus and on the vertex; abdominal tergites almost entirely smooth with one row of marginal bristles, the sternites additionally hairy. Head oval; nasus nearly cylindrical in front, conical and widened at the base in lateral view; the elevation at the base of the nasus distinct. Antennae 13-segmented: segment 3 longer than segment 2; segment 4 slightly shorter than segment 2. Front of the pronotum upturned almost at a right angle, anterior margin not concave.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head brown; anterior angles of the transverse band, clypeus, base of the mandibles, labrum and the region around the antennae rusty yellow; sagittal suture white; legs and body sclerites rusty yellow. Head with extremely fine hairs; abdominal tergites hairy with a few long marginal bristles (the bristles on the tergites short). Head broadly oval, widest at the level of the antennae; sagittal suture open; transverse suture almost entirely closed; fontanelle elongate-triangular; clypeal sclerite short and rather strongly convex, the convexity not reaching the medium-sized mandibular condyles. Antennae 14-segmented: segment 3 about equal to segment 2 or slightly longer; segment 4 distinctly shorter than segment 2.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: The original was published as Eutermes mojosensis n. sp.; figure 20 shows the queen's head and the soldier's head; the species is one of those in the genus for which the variation curves of soldier head length and head width were measured specimen by specimen (51 specimens).
